projects.name: WallBaduk
projects.subtitle: From a solo mobile launch to a stronger game AI
projects.role: Planning · Design · Model training & game AI · App & multiplayer development · Release
projects.summary: I designed and shipped a 7×7 strategy game on both app stores in three weeks. I then trained a game AI, ran it inside the mobile app, and used real match losses to improve the engine.
projects.problem: The bot had to choose a legal move and wall placement together within a mobile search budget. In real matches, the evaluator rewarded getting boxed into a single square, and the search sometimes discarded the opponent’s critical blocking reply.
contributions: Built the Flutter game and its rule engine, including move and wall validation, territory separation, and win detection. Used Firestore to synchronize games joined by room code or automatic matchmaking.

Encoded the board as seven channels and checked for action-index collisions across 3,185 move-and-wall combinations. Trained a 3,554-parameter policy–value CNN from completed game records, then refined it with PPO against search bots and earlier policies.

Implemented on-device inference in Dart and used model scores to guide candidate ordering and evaluation. Expert and Sedol share weights and use different search breadth and time budgets. I kept the game’s rules authoritative for terminal outcomes.

Reproduced losses from real matches and revised the evaluator to account for each cell’s accessibility. I kept tactical blocking replies in the candidate set and re-searched positions where a critical reply could have been omitted.
projects.outcome: Shipped the first app on iOS and Android in three weeks and later released the Expert and Sedol neural search update on both stores. In a separate 192-game follow-up benchmark on unseen starting layouts, with model weights held constant, Expert won 46 of 48 and Sedol won 44 of 48 against their previous versions.

metric.label: From planning to release on both stores

projects.name: STABLE
projects.subtitle: Improving attribute binding with visual evidence
projects.role: First author · Method design · Implementation & experiments · Writing
projects.summary: As first author, I designed and implemented an inference-time intervention that uses a multimodal model’s internal visual evidence to improve how it pairs attributes with objects.
projects.problem: A model can recognize both a black plate and an orange napkin yet swap their colors in its answer. I examined attention and hidden states across layers to locate visual evidence for the correct pairings.
contributions: Analyzed attention and hidden states across layers and estimated relative visual correspondence between attribute and object tokens.
Used agreement between syntactic and visual associations to calibrate a steering direction, then applied it during a single forward pass per caption with model weights frozen.
Implemented adapters for Qwen2-VL-7B and LLaVA-1.5-7B, separated calibration and evaluation data, and ran four benchmark suites and ablations to assess the effect of the intervention.
projects.outcome: The submission reports 73.00% ColorSwap Group accuracy on LLaVA-1.5-7B, up from 67.33% with VQAScore. On 100 ARO samples using LLaVA-1.5 on a TITAN RTX, it took 0.60 seconds per sample, 4.1× faster than CRG and 25.6× faster than COCO-Tree. Submitted to ICASSP 2027 and under review.

projects.name: Mote
projects.subtitle: Korean speech recognition, diarization & compression
projects.role: AI development · Dataset curation · Training & evaluation · API integration
projects.summary: I fine-tuned Whisper for Korean speech and domain-specific terminology, then built the pipeline that turns a meeting recording into a speaker-labeled transcript and structured summary.
projects.problem: Meetings contained technical vocabulary and multiple speakers. The app also needed a speech model that could run on CPU and an API response the backend could consume.
contributions: Aligned Korean subtitles with audio, resampled the recordings to 16 kHz, and filtered short clips. Built software development and economics datasets for additional fine-tuning, then selected checkpoints by word error rate.
Combined x-vector embeddings with spectral clustering to identify speaker segments. Transcribed each segment, attached speaker labels, and passed the transcript to an LLM for structured summaries.

Converted and quantized Whisper with CTranslate2 for faster-whisper CPU inference. Implemented S3 recording input and a JSON result API, then worked with the backend developer to connect it to the app.
projects.outcome: Reduced the model file from 3.2 GB to 820 MB, published models and datasets on Hugging Face, and integrated speaker-labeled transcription and meeting summaries into the app.

projects.name: StarGAN-TA
projects.subtitle: Transfer learning for facial expression generation
projects.role: Preprocessing · Model adaptation · Experiments · Co-authored paper
projects.summary: I worked with my co-authors to transfer pretrained StarGAN weights to a six-expression task, from face preprocessing and model changes through experiments and paper writing.
projects.problem: The pretrained generator and discriminator expected five attributes. Adding a sixth expression changed the layer dimensions and prevented the original weights from loading directly.
contributions: Worked jointly on face detection, cropping and resizing, model adaptation, experiments, and the paper.

Expanded the generator input to RGB plus six condition channels and rebuilt the discriminator’s classification layer. We kept compatible pretrained weights and initialized the new input channel with the mean of the original attribute channels.
In a separate 2024 code update, I changed the generator’s activations from ReLU to LeakyReLU and reorganized the training code and runtime setup.
projects.outcome: Co-authored “StarGAN-TA: Transfer Learning with StarGAN for Improved Facial Expression Generation,” published in the ICROS 2023 conference proceedings.

projects.name: Lenfit
projects.subtitle: Real-time exercise feedback & repetition counting
projects.role: Pose assessment · Repetition counting · Backend integration
projects.summary: I built exercise repetition and form-feedback logic that converts pose estimates into valid reps and corrective cues.
projects.problem: Pose coordinates fluctuated between frames, and a shallow squat could look like a completed rep. Recording clips also needed to start after the user returned to the starting pose.
contributions: Built a Python prototype on MediaPipe’s pose classification example. Connected squat and push-up samples, widened the gap between entry and exit thresholds, and retained the current count when a pose was missing.
Used an exponential moving average of classification scores to check for a return to the starting pose before opening the next exercise clip.

For the app, defined feedback and counting rules using ML Kit joint angles, positions, and movement direction. A squat that reversed upward too soon triggered a correction and was excluded from the rep count. Worked with the backend developer on integration.
projects.outcome: Delivered real-time form feedback and valid-rep counting for Lenfit, a team project in Hanium ICT Mentoring.

projects.name: Diff-SVC × DiffWave
projects.subtitle: Singing voice conversion with limited-data augmentation
projects.role: Audio preprocessing & augmentation · Diff-SVC training & experiments
projects.summary: I prepared singing audio, trained voice conversion models for multiple singers, and used DiffWave to supplement recordings for singers with fewer samples.
projects.problem: Available recordings varied by singer, and some targets had too little usable audio after segmentation and silence removal.
contributions: Standardized audio formats, segmented recordings, and removed long silences for Diff-SVC training. Prepared inputs by aligning HuBERT features and F0 with mel frames.
Conditioned DiffWave on mel spectrograms from the original recordings and combined the generated audio with real samples to train Diff-SVC.
Worked with the other AI developer to set up an original-only baseline and an augmented-data condition, then compared the resulting conversions for the same target voice.
projects.outcome: Completed model training and voice conversion with augmented data for multiple target singers. The team integrated the models, iOS app, and server into a singing voice conversion program.

projects.name: RESTED
projects.subtitle: Cognitive rehabilitation quizzes & AI models
projects.role: Quiz design · Model training · Team collaboration & service integration
projects.summary: I built object-finding and emotion-recognition quizzes by connecting an object detector and a facial expression generator to answer checking and session records.
projects.problem: The object detector could miss an item during an answer attempt, and generated faces could appear corrupted when handed to the quiz interface.
contributions: Fine-tuned an object detector for everyday objects in Korean homes. Built a quiz that selects a target from the camera view, checks the item the user presents, and retries up to five times when no item is detected.

Fine-tuned StarGAN on six emotion classes from AI Hub and generated expressions from photos of familiar people. Fixed corrupted images by rearranging the output tensor into HWC order, converting it to uint8, and correcting how the image buffer was passed.
Recorded quiz targets, answers, scores, and completion times in date-keyed JSON and worked with teammates to integrate and demonstrate the rehabilitation program.
projects.outcome: The team completed and demonstrated RESTED and won the Grand Prize in the Intelligent Mechatronics Engineering division at Sejong University’s 2023 Creative Design Competition.

projects.name: WriteNow
projects.subtitle: GPT fine-tuning & document automation
projects.role: Document sample collection · Input/output dataset curation · GPT fine-tuning
projects.summary: I fine-tuned GPT to extract fields from Word forms and built the document-processing pipeline that turns app answers into completed forms.
projects.problem: The model’s responses did not consistently match the JSON schema the app needed for text fields and choices. The resulting answers also had to land in the right cells and checkboxes in the original template.
contributions: Collected document samples and built training pairs from Word table text and structured JSON targets. Preserved row and column order in the text and fine-tuned GPT through the OpenAI API.
Wrote rules that normalize labels such as Name and its equivalents, find the matching cells, and fill in answers or mark selected choices while retaining the template.

Implemented Flask endpoints for template and signature uploads and document generation. Generated DOCX files, converted them to PDF, and placed signature images at the designated marker. Worked with the backend developer to connect the flow to the app.
projects.outcome: Completed the team workflow from template upload and in-app questions to completed Word forms and signed PDF output.

projects.name: Souf
projects.subtitle: Launched and operated a student freelancer platform
projects.role: Founder & CEO · Product planning · Development leadership · Operations
projects.summary: I founded Souf, led its launch, and built tools that the team used to automate recurring work during platform operations.
projects.problem: Students needed a way to move from showcasing their work to discussing terms and drafting a contract. Once the platform launched, collecting and posting new opportunities and preparing contracts also took recurring manual effort.
contributions: As founder and CEO, I defined portfolio posts, real-time chat, and contract drafting as the core product flow. I coordinated the team’s development work and registered the business with support from Sejong University’s Campus Town program.
Built and used an operations tool that collected opportunities, categorized listings, merged duplicates by title, and separated active from expired posts for publishing.
Built and used a contract generator that filled paragraphs and tables in Word templates from JSON and exported the resulting documents as PDFs.
projects.outcome: Launched and operated the freelancer platform. Separately planned AI portfolio generation as a follow-up feature and prepared data for its development.
